title: Thompson, Ritchie, and the First Unix Kernel on a PDP-7 (1969-70)
explainer: xv6 is a teaching reimplementation of the Sixth Edition Unix kernel, and its design - a small resident kernel, a process table, a simple file system - traces back to the original Unix kernel Ken Thompson wrote in assembly on a scavenged PDP-7 in 1969, right after Bell Labs withdrew from the sprawling Multics project. Unix's deliberate smallness was a direct reaction against Multics's complexity, a philosophy still visible in xv6's roughly ten thousand lines of kernel code.
